title: The stability cubic at $q = 1.1100$: lattice points and the nuclear chart
html:
At q = q_0, the stability cubic (Diophantine valley) parametrises the valley of stability:

  t^3 =  2p(1 + ct^2),
  \qquad c = 0.01497, \quad A = t^3

See Table.

The predicted neutron number N_{\mathrm{pred}} minimizes the convex quadratic E(p, A) (integer stability). The discrepancy \Delta N = |N_{\mathrm{pred}} - N_{\mathrm{obs}}| is zero up to iron, and at most 2 everywhere.

The Coulomb term a_C \cdot p^2/A^{1/3} penalizes proton-rich nuclei. Driven entirely by q_0, the neutron excess grows from 0\% at hydrogen to 59\% at uranium.
